latest_findings.claim: With m2 fixed at 0.5 and N=64, fresh seeds 22 and 23 decode force well above control. From probes_final at layer 1, trained force R2 is 0.767/0.770 against control 0.574/0.542, giving margins of 0.193/0.228 against a required 0.1. That matches the force R2 of m2-fixed seeds 20-21 (0.763/0.789). accel_step peaks at layer 4 with R2 0.932/0.938 against control 0.729/0.744, a raw margin of 0.202/0.193 and a headroom-normalised margin of 0.747/0.756, so force leads on raw margin while accel_step leads on normalised margin.
latest_findings.confidence_note: Both seeds completed all 3000 planned steps and beat the baseline (val_mse_ratio 0.0131/0.0130). Each seed independently meets the force-margin, trained-R2 and accel_step criteria. One pre-registered criterion was missed: seed 23's force control R2 is 0.542, just below the stated [0.55, 0.68] range. I still call the verdict supported because the miss does not change it. With the control at 0.55, seed 23's margin would be about 0.22, and seed 22 alone meets every criterion. The low control does make the margin less comparable: seed 23's 0.228 is larger than seeds 20-21's 0.133/0.195 mainly because its control is lower. Trained R2 is the tighter statistic here (0.763-0.789 across all four m2-fixed seeds), while control R2 ranges from 0.54 to 0.63. All four seeds share data_seed 0, so dataset variance is untested. Force is still rising at step 3000 (about +0.010 per 500 steps), and its best layer moves from 4 to 1 at steps 1000-1500, so the final level depends on training length. These are the N=64 reference values, not a test of the N trend. The verdict would change if another data_seed gave force margin < 0.1 or trained R2 < 0.68 at N=64 with m2 fixed.

latest_findings.claim: With m2 fixed at 0.5, N=128 models on seeds 22-23 do not decode force above control. Force R2 is 0.654 (layer 4, control 0.592, margin 0.062) and 0.631 (layer 1, control 0.551, margin 0.080), both below the required 0.1. accel_step stays strong: R2 0.920/0.936, controls 0.715/0.736, headroom-normalised margin 0.72/0.76. Against the paired N=64 m2-fixed arm (seeds 22/23: best-layer force margin 0.193/0.228 at layer 1; trajectory force R2 about 0.767/0.770; control about 0.57/0.54), trained force R2 drops about 0.11/0.14 and the force control changes by only about +0.02/+0.01. That replicates the seeds 20-21 pattern: the force drop is in trained R2, not in the control.
latest_findings.confidence_note: Both runs completed all 3000 steps and beat the baseline (val_mse_ratio 0.062/0.053). The pre-registered pairing reads N=64 values from probes_final, but the paired arm's probes_final was not available to this analysis, so its trained R2 and control come from the probe_trajectory. The 4th trajectory field may be max-over-layers R2 rather than the best-margin-layer R2 (q-20261013-075749-57bb). In these N=128 runs it overstates probes_final by 0.003-0.006. The trained-R2 drop does not depend much on this: the margins alone fall by 0.13-0.15, and a drop under 0.05 would need the N=64 control to sit about 0.08 or more below its trajectory-implied value. The control criterion (|change| <= 0.03) is the fragile part. It is met only approximately (+0.018/+0.009), and for seed 22 the controls come from different layers (layer 4 at N=128, layer 1 at N=64). Two things would change the verdict: probes_final for the N=64 arm showing a control rise of 0.03 or more in either seed, or a same-layer control comparison doing so. Matching on step also confounds convergence: N=64 is further converged at step 3000, so a matched-loss comparison might shrink the gap. With seeds 20-21 there are now four m2-fixed seeds that all show a trained-R2 drop of 0.07-0.14.

latest_findings.claim: With m2 fixed at 0.5 and N=256, accel_step clearly beats its control in both seeds: layer 4, R2 0.912/0.923 vs control 0.686/0.681, headroom-normalised margin 0.72/0.76. Force does not beat its control in either seed: seed 22 margin 0.002 at layer 0 (R2 0.166 vs control 0.164), seed 23 margin 0.094 at layer 1 (R2 0.666 vs control 0.572, needs 0.1). The force-control comparison with N=128, which is the actual hypothesis, cannot be computed reliably: seed 22's best force layer at N=256 is layer 0, which has no counterpart in the N=128 arm (layer 4), and the N=128 m2-fixed seeds 22-23 arm (exp-20261014-001210-53d8) has no probes_final available, only max-over-layers trajectories.
latest_findings.confidence_note: Both runs completed all 3000 steps and beat the baseline (val_mse_ratio 0.201/0.211). The accel_step half of the expected-if-true outcome is met in both seeds. The force-control half is not computed, as the hypothesis requires when the paired arm is unavailable. This run shows that the trajectory's 4th field is the max R2 over layers: seed 22 shows 0.604 there vs probes_final R2 0.166 at layer 0. So 'R2 minus margin' from the N=128 trajectories does not give a control R2 at a fixed layer. For seed 23 alone, a rough trajectory-derived N=128 control at layer 1 (0.637 - 0.080 = about 0.557) would give a change of about +0.015, which falls in the 'no rise' range. That number is unreliable and comes from one seed. Seed 22 cannot be compared, because its N=256 best-margin layer is 0. Per-seed force margins across N are 0.193 -> 0.062 -> 0.002 for seed 22 and 0.228 -> 0.080 -> 0.094 for seed 23. That gives N=64 > N=128 for both seeds, but N=128 > N=256 for seed 22 only, consistent with the large model-seed variance in force seen before at N=256. Seed 23's N=256 force margin is still rising (+0.005 to +0.009 per 500 steps) and sits just below the bar. The verdict would change with probes_final, or per-layer controls, at a fixed layer for the N=128 m2-fixed seeds 22-23 runs. If both seeds then showed |control change| <= 0.02, it becomes supported. If both showed >= +0.03, it becomes refuted.

latest_findings.claim: With m2 fixed at 0.5, the N=64 to N=128 drop in trained force R2 does not go away. At N=128 (best layer 4), trained force R2 is 0.693 (seed 20) and 0.684 (seed 21), against 0.763 and 0.789 for the same seeds in the paired N=64 m2-fixed arm. That is a drop of 0.070 and 0.105, close to the wide-m2 drop of 0.08-0.13. The force controls barely move (seed 20: about 0.63 to 0.630; seed 21: about 0.594 to 0.583, change of 0.012 or less), so the whole drop is in trained R2. The force margin falls from 0.133/0.195 to 0.063/0.101, and seed 20 no longer beats its control. In contrast, accel_step stays strong: R2 0.945/0.933 vs control 0.793/0.760, margin 0.152/0.173, headroom-normalised margin 0.74/0.72. Layer-1 distance R2 falls only a little (0.950/0.926 to 0.915/0.908). The force loss at N=128 is therefore in reading out 1/r^2, not in the m2 factor.
latest_findings.confidence_note: Both seeds completed all 3000 steps and both show a drop of at least 0.06 with flat controls, which matches the expected-if-false outcome. The N=64 baseline values (0.763/0.789) come from the paired arm's earlier finding, not from probes_final of this experiment. The paired-arm trajectory gives 0.768 for seed 20, which may be the max-over-layers field. N=64 controls were inferred as R2 minus margin. Seed 20's drop (0.070) is only 0.01 above the 0.06 bar, so a probes_final N=64 value below 0.753 would make that seed inconclusive. The best layers also differ for seed 21: force peaks at layer 1 (the distance layer) at N=64 and at layer 4 at N=128, so part of the drop may be a layer-1 force signal that disappears. The comparison is at matched training step, not matched loss (N=128 val_mse_ratio is 0.048-0.056). The verdict would change if the drop shrinks below 0.03 when both arms are read at matched val_mse_ratio, or if more seeds (22-23) show drops under 0.06.

latest_findings.claim: With m2 fixed at 0.5, the N=256 force random-control R2 is 0.6197 (seed 20, layer 1) and 0.6521 (seed 21, layer 3). The paired N=128 m2-fixed arm has no probes_final yet, so the planned comparison was not computed. Its trajectory gives controls of at most about 0.633 (seed 20) and 0.583 (seed 21), which suggests the seeds disagree: about -0.013 or more for seed 20 and about +0.069 or more for seed 21. Separately, trained force fails to beat control at N=256 in both seeds (R2 0.648 vs control 0.620, margin 0.028; R2 0.655 vs control 0.652, margin 0.003), while accel_step clears the bar easily (R2 0.935 vs control 0.770, margin 0.165, normalised 0.72; R2 0.930 vs control 0.716, margin 0.213, normalised 0.75). Force margin falls with N in both seeds even with m2 fixed (N=64 0.133/0.195, N=128 0.063/0.101, N=256 0.028/0.003, from trajectories).
latest_findings.confidence_note: The hypothesis said to read the N=128 control from probes_final and to report the comparison as not computed if that was unavailable. It is unavailable because exp-20261013-231210-ae2c is still analyzing. The N=128 controls above were worked out as trajectory R2 minus margin. That trajectory R2 is a max over layers, not the R2 at the best-margin layer: for this experiment's own runs it reads 0.657/0.665 against probes_final 0.648/0.655. So the derived N=128 controls are upper bounds that may be about 0.01 too high, and the per-seed rises are lower bounds. Seed 21 clears the +0.03 bar even under that bias. Seed 20 could fall anywhere from below the N=128 value up into the 0.01-0.03 inconclusive band. The best-margin layer also differs between arms (N=256 layers 1/3 vs N=128 layer 4), so the controls are not compared at the same layer. Control spread is 0.022-0.030, close to the size of the effect being tested. Only 2 seeds and 1 data_seed. Both runs completed 3000/3000 steps and beat the baseline (val_mse_ratio 0.196/0.243). The accel_step part of the true-prediction is met in both seeds (margin >= 0.1, normalised 0.72/0.75 inside [0.55, 0.85]). What would change the verdict: once the N=128 m2-fixed probes_final exist, a supported verdict needs seed 20's control to be <= 0.590, and a refuted verdict needs seed 21's to be >= 0.642. The trajectory bound already makes the second unlikely.
